report_name: Two Ransomware Gangs, GENESIS and Anubis, Claim Breach of Interim HealthCare

threat_actors.name: GENESIS
threat_actors.description: A ransomware group that claimed to have breached Interim HealthCare on August 10, 2026. The group alleged the theft of approximately 1 terabyte of data, including patient medical records, from locations in Oklahoma City and Tulsa.
threat_actors.goals: Financial extortion through ransomware and data exfiltration.

threat_actors.name: Anubis
threat_actors.description: A ransomware group that claimed to have breached Interim HealthCare on August 21, 2026, eleven days after a similar claim by the GENESIS group. Anubis alleged the exfiltration of 530 gigabytes of corporate data and began leaking samples to extort the victim.
threat_actors.goals: Financial extortion through ransomware and data exfiltration.

attack_patterns.name: Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol
attack_patterns.description: Used as part of a double extortion strategy by both GENESIS and Anubis to steal sensitive data from the victim's network before encryption.

attack_patterns.name: Data Encrypted for Impact
attack_patterns.description: Used by the ransomware groups to encrypt files on Interim HealthCare's systems to cause operational disruption and demand a ransom.

attack_patterns.name: Data Destruction
attack_patterns.description: Anubis Ransomware reportedly includes an optional "wipe mode" that can permanently destroy files, even if a ransom is paid.

attack_patterns.name: Inhibit System Recovery
attack_patterns.description: Ransomware actors commonly delete volume shadow copies using tools like vssadmin to prevent easy restoration of encrypted files.

malware.name: Anubis Ransomware
malware.description: A ransomware variant used by the Anubis group to target Interim HealthCare. It is noted for being particularly destructive, featuring an optional "wipe mode" to permanently destroy files.

tools.name: vssadmin
tools.description: The vssadmin tool is likely used by the ransomware to delete shadow copies, inhibiting system recovery from encrypted files.

identities.name: Interim HealthCare
identities.description: A leading U.S. provider of home care and healthcare staffing services that was the target of a double-extortion ransomware attack by the GENESIS and Anubis groups.

infrastructure.name: GENESIS Leak Site
infrastructure.description: A dark web site used by the GENESIS ransomware group to publish claims of breaches and threaten or leak stolen data.

infrastructure.name: Anubis Leak Site
infrastructure.description: A dark web site used by the Anubis ransomware group to publish claims, leak data samples, and extort victims like Interim HealthCare.

indicators.name: VSSAdmin Shadow Copy Deletion
indicators.pattern:
title: VSSAdmin Shadow Copy Deletion
id: 7b8a1c2d-e3f4-4a5b-8c6d-7e8f9a0b1c2d
status: experimental
description: Detects the use of vssadmin.exe to delete volume shadow copies, a common technique used by ransomware to inhibit system recovery.
references:
  - https://shattered.io/two-ransomware-gangs-claim-interim-healthcare-2026/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-09-11
tags:
  - attack.t1490
  - attack.impact
level: high
logsource:
  product: windows
  category: process_creation
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\vssadmin.exe'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - 'delete'
      - 'shadows'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the use of vssadmin.exe to delete volume shadow copies, a common ransomware technique mentioned as a hunting hint in the report.
